## Summary

A convergence test that RE-DERIVES what the send path does — instead of DRIVING the send path
and capturing what it produced — measures the helper it named, not the convergence it claims.
It stays green when the send path drifts, which is the only failure it exists to catch.

This has now happened **twice in the same module**, and the second time it was caught only
because a code reviewer flagged it as a non-blocking advisory:

1. `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/mutate/test_outbound_comment_length_convergence.py` modelled
   the landed Jira body as `comment_limits.truncate_comment_body(emitted_body)`. When
   `emersed-specific-mutt` moved the Cloud send path onto `AdfCodec.fit_outbound`, that model
   went stale and the test kept passing while live convergence was broken — the divergence
   later filed as `abusive-pebbly-sakimonkey` and paid for in 836 unmarked duplicate comments
   in live Jira.
2. The FIRST version of that ticket's own fix carried the same flaw: its oracle computed the
   send side as `fit_preserving_marker(_decorate_outbound_comment(body), codec.fit_outbound)`
   — a copy of the composition under test. **It passed Gerrit CI with `Verified +1`.** Seeding
   `emersed-specific-mutt`'s exact mistake back into `add_comment` left it GREEN.

## Runtime evidence

Mutation applied to `acli_cli_ops.add_comment`, reverting it to the drifted form:

```
body_arg = json.dumps(codec.to_wire(fit_preserving_marker(body, codec.fit_outbound)))
       ->  json.dumps(codec.to_wire(codec.fit_outbound(body)))

re-derived oracle : 8 passed     <- blind to the regression it is named for
captured oracle   : 2 failed     <- detects it
```

The fix was to capture the `--body` argument from a real `acli_cli_ops.add_comment` call with
only `acli_subprocess._run_acli` stubbed, so the send side of the assertion moves with the send
path rather than with a copy of it.

## Why a ticket and not a comment

Nothing in the repo distinguishes the two shapes. Both read as "the differ agrees with the send
path"; only one is true. `make lint`, the complexity ratchet, the mutation gate and the code
review all passed the re-derived version, and the review that did notice could only file it as
advisory.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Decide and record the rule for convergence tests in this codebase: the side representing
      an external effect must be captured from the real call site, not recomputed from the
      helpers that call site uses.
- [ ] The rule is discoverable where a test author will hit it (the test-design guidance the
      debug/implement skills already point at), with the two instances above as worked examples.
- [ ] Evaluate whether a mechanical check is feasible — e.g. flagging a test that imports the
      same fit/encode helper the module under test uses on both sides of an equality assertion
      — and either add it or record why it is not worth the false-positive cost.
compiled_state.title: Convergence tests re-derive the send path instead of driving it
